hook: There has never been any lead inside a pencil.

blocks.narration: There has never been any lead inside a pencil. What you are actually writing with is a mix of graphite and clay.
blocks.visual: Photoreal macro shot of a sharpened pencil tip on white paper, slow push-in, clean industrial light

blocks.narration: In the fifteen hundreds, a huge graphite deposit was found in England. People thought it was lead, and the name stuck.
blocks.visual: Cinematic shot of dark glittering graphite rock in a misty English hillside quarry

blocks.narration: In a factory today, powdered graphite is mixed with clay and water into a thick paste, like dark gray dough.
blocks.visual: Macro shot of an industrial mixer churning dark gray paste, satisfying slow motion

blocks.narration: The paste is pushed through a small opening into long thin rods, cut to length, dried, and then fired in a hot kiln.
blocks.visual: Thin dark rods extrude smoothly from a machine and glide onto a tray, glowing kiln in background

blocks.narration: Here is the clever part. More clay makes a harder, lighter pencil. More graphite makes a softer, darker one.
blocks.visual: Two pencil lines drawn side by side on paper, one pale and crisp, one dark and rich

blocks.narration: Meanwhile, thin slats of cedar wood get rows of tiny grooves cut into them. The rods are laid into those grooves.
blocks.visual: Macro shot of a cutter carving parallel grooves into a cedar slat, wood shavings curling

blocks.narration: A second grooved slat is glued on top like a sandwich. Then a machine slices the sandwich into individual pencils.
blocks.visual: A wooden sandwich slides into a cutter and emerges as a neat row of hexagonal pencils

blocks.narration: Finally they get painted, stamped, and topped with an eraser. Comment what everyday object we should break down next.
blocks.visual: Freshly painted pencils roll down a conveyor in perfect rows, satisfying final wide shot

cta: Comment what everyday object we should break down next.

captions.hook_line: There has never been any lead in a pencil. Here's what's actually inside ✏️
captions.body: Pencil 'lead' is graphite mixed with clay, fired in a kiln and sandwiched between grooved wooden slats. More clay makes a harder, lighter line; more graphite makes a softer, darker one.
